svg.text: One kernel, three schedulings — threads, worlds and crossings by host mode (AS BUILT)

✔ built on exp/threaded-build (overnight 2026-11-12/13, N-1…N-17) · ⏳ in flight (R-4218 the mode, R-4220 the review source, the serial systems). Numbers: Debug, 4-core VM, 1 000 men; Windows Release numbers pending (CE-4489).
the UI on the main thread, the simulation on ONE sim worker
no presentation; the tick on the process's main thread
③ DETERMINISTIC — stepped, Run-to, filming, regression, tests
same threads as ① or ②; chosen by what is running (R-4218 ⏳)
never waits for a tick, no lock: UI frame ≈ 45 ms at 1 / 2 / 4 threads
pull ≈ 4–5 ms, only when a newer tick is complete
two staging buffers claimed by CAS; both busy ⇒ skip, the next
publish carries it all (R-4217) · publish ≈ 4 ms · 0 skips measured
--mode all: EVERY kernel of the process on this one worker ✔
≈ 800 ms of the tick still serial — the next conversions ⏳
no main-thread presentation · no world A
no staging, no job queue — nothing paid for a UI
the ONE thread that writes S; no locks in the tick
Windows: EcoQoS / power throttling OFF, QuickEdit off ✔ (N-14)
the same per-entity phases as ①
own entity written directly; others by command,
played in batch order; their data read from the tick-start view
windowed: as ① — the UI still never waits for a tick
tests and rails: INLINE (HROT_THREADED_SINGLE=1 runs the
same sim step, pull and presentation step on one thread)
✔ the SAME world at 1, 2, 4, 8 threads — 7 stepped runs, 1 000 men
one value for the whole process (R-4215), set from the clock (R-4218 ⏳)
fixed 32-entity batches, buffers played in batch order = entity order ✔
Throughput (continuous live play): adaptive batch size — the same rule
a result that differs by batch size or thread count is a BUG,
never a reason for a mode (R-4218)
The strategies — what holds in every mode
S — the simulation, ONE writer (the sim worker and its pool) · A — the UI's world, ONE writer (the main thread), the same object for life · B1 / B2 — two staging buffers (102 MB at 1 000 men) ·
the tick-start view (11 MB) for cross-entity reads · R — the replica for off-frame egress; the recorder captures on the tick and writes its file asynchronously
DOWN: one SimJobQueue — UI writes, run controls, sim-side HTTP, the UI's bus publishes, review commands (R-4220 ⏳) · UP: the staging — masked tables (the active gizmo layers), the selected rows,
singletons, and a tick-tagged packet FIFO: events, logs, edit outcomes, undo steps, the bus pair, readouts — exactly once, in order
buffers claimed by compare-and-swap; the sim never waits — both busy ⇒ it skips that publish (R-4217) · the UI pulls only a newer complete tick · inside the tick per-batch command buffers, never a
managed components are immutable and replaced whole (audit: 6 in-place sites, the traffic frame fixed and value-copied) · a managed read never stamps (R-4210) · shared objects immutable or swapped
in one write · derived maps rebuilt · values only the sim can compute are published as readouts
the WHOLE gizmo block on the main thread over A (R-4211) · a drag is a ghost in A, the drop one job through the shared write router; refused ⇒ snap back · undo: the recorder on S, the ONE history
on the UI · UI-side HTTP routes read the shown world
OWN entity (its parts; a squad job its members) read and written directly · ANOTHER entity: declared types from the tick-start view, declared stable reads live · writes to others, add / remove /
create / destroy, publishes ⇒ the batch's buffer, played in batch order · callouts, egress marks, rule messages ⇒ follow-ups in batch order · HROT_READ_CHECK=1 throws on an undeclared read, =2
ONE pool (frame lane + background lane), no dependency scheduler · ParallelEntities.Run: 32-entity batches carrying the tick context and the current entity · EQS's window sized by the same budget
· switches: HROT_THREADED_KERNEL=3 · HROT_PARALLEL_SIM=1 · HROT_SIM_THREADS — all OFF by default, 0 B per steady frame
What each mode pays — nothing it does not use
